source: Canonical product/security/database specs, ADRs, Word references and live GitHub backlog review
note: AI-drafted planning backlog. October working estimate is 180 hours after adding 24 explicit database-foundation hours. Replan capacity before committing to October 31; acceptance gates remain mandatory. Post-MVP candidates are not release commitments.

epics.title: Disposable public prototype
epics.outcome: A public demo URL shows the intended guest and host flow without real accounts or transfers

stories.title: Deploy static demo
stories.story: As a founder, I want a temporary public URL so that I can show the prototype to hosts and guests.
acceptance: The root URL loads the guest landing page on mobile and desktop.
The prototype is served over HTTPS and can be deleted without affecting future production.

stories.title: Make demo boundaries visible
stories.story: As a visitor, I want to know this is a demo so that I do not try to send money or enter sensitive data.
acceptance: Every payment control states no app opens and no transfer occurs.
Sample host identifiers and non-persistent content are clearly labeled.

stories.title: Make the demo link shareable
stories.story: As a founder, I want the Copy link button to use the deployed URL so that testers reach the live prototype.
acceptance: Copied URL opens the guest landing page.
A decorative QR is not presented as a scannable QR.

stories.title: Review the prototype on phones
stories.story: As a founder, I want to test the flow on a phone so that screens are usable at an event.
acceptance: Guest and host navigation, service picker, card editor and book preview work at common mobile widths.
Keyboard focus and button labels remain visible.

stories.title: Capture tester feedback
stories.story: As a founder, I want a simple feedback checklist so that the first hosted demo teaches us what to build.
acceptance: Record task completion, confusion points and wrong-payee concerns.
Convert validated findings to backlog issues before MVP implementation.

epics.title: Identity and access
epics.outcome: Hosts control private event data while guests can contribute through scoped sessions

stories.title: Managed host sign-in
stories.story: As a host, I want to sign in securely so that I can manage my event.
acceptance: Use a managed identity provider and verified email.
Server stores provider subject and role, not a custom password database.
Persist one identity.customers record per (auth_issuer, auth_subject); synchronize verified email without using email as ownership identity or storing passwords.

Review Apple, Google, Amazon and manual email account entry with an account-free UI bypass during design review; provider eligibility/configuration and verified server sessions remain required before launch. Never collect a password in the local UI.

stories.title: Enforce event ownership
stories.story: As a host, I want only authorized hosts to see my private event data so that gifts and notes remain private.
acceptance: Every host read and write checks ownership or explicit membership on the server.
Cross-event access tests are denied.
Resolve ownership from events.events.owner_customer_id and verified customer identity; scoped database interfaces/policies deny cross-event data using actual runtime credentials.

stories.title: Protect sensitive host actions
stories.story: As a host, I want a fresh sign-in for payment destination edits and exports so that stolen sessions have less power.
acceptance: Require step-up authentication on sensitive actions.
Log actor, event, action and time.
Append minimal platform.audit_events for sensitive actions; no token, destination identifier or private text in audit payloads.

stories.title: Issue scoped guest sessions
stories.story: As a guest, I want to leave a note without an account so that contributing is easy.
acceptance: Issue a short-lived event-scoped session and store only its token hash.
A guest cannot read or edit another guest’s private draft.
Persist identity.event_guests independently of identity.guest_sessions, with same-event guest/link FKs; session expiry/revocation cannot delete accepted cards or gift records.

stories.title: Alert hosts to destination changes
stories.story: As a host, I want notice when a payment account changes so that I can catch unauthorized edits.
acceptance: Send a change alert containing service and change time without sensitive secrets.
Keep old and new route versions in an audit trail.
Queue alerts through platform.outbox_messages in the route-change transaction; audit references immutable destination versions without copying identifiers.

stories.title: Separate operator privileges
stories.story: As an operator, I want limited support access so that production support does not expose unrelated private data.
acceptance: Support roles use multifactor authentication and least privilege.
Private note access is audited and not available by default.

epics.title: Event pages, links and time windows
epics.outcome: One stable event URL supports the full contribution and gift lifecycle

stories.title: Create dated event or occasion
stories.story: As a host, I want to enter an event date, time zone and page type so that the opening and closing dates are accurate.
acceptance: Server derives allowed windows in the event time zone.
An undated one-off page must choose a close date within 90 days.
Persist events.events with owner, occasion label, lifecycle kind, IANA timezone, derived UTC deadlines and policy version; only wedding kind grants the month-12 extension.

stories.title: Publish one shareable URL
stories.story: As a host, I want one link that I can text or email so that remote guests reach the event.
acceptance: Generate an opaque, unguessable slug.
Public page exposes only approved event fields.
Persist events.share_links with unique token hash, encrypted recoverable secret and generation; enforce one unrevoked link per event.

Guest pages are invitation-only, with no public event directory or guest-event link in public navigation; host preview uses the same event route. Frontend routing never substitutes for server link authorization.

stories.title: Generate QR from the same URL
stories.story: As a host, I want a printable QR so that in-person guests reach the same page.
acceptance: QR encodes only the stable event URL, never a wallet identifier.
Scanning and clicking return the same event state.

stories.title: Open no earlier than six months
stories.story: As a host, I want to open contributions up to six months before the event so that guests can participate early.
acceptance: Scheduled pages reject new notes, cards, art jobs and gift intents before opens_at.
Guest sees the opening state.

stories.title: Close book contributions after day 90
stories.story: As a host, I want new notes, cards and photos to stop 90 days after the event so that the book can be finalized.
acceptance: Server rejects these writes after the boundary.
Existing private content and export remain available to the host.

stories.title: Keep late wedding gifts open
stories.story: As a guest, I want a gift-only route through month 12 after a wedding so that I can give late without changing the book.
acceptance: Only new gifts are permitted after day 90 and through month 12.
Non-wedding events close gift intake at day 90.

stories.title: Show a closed landing page
stories.story: As a visitor, I want a clear closed message so that I do not attempt an unavailable action.
acceptance: Old link and QR still open a closed page.
No new card or gift intent can be initiated after final close.

stories.title: Prevent deadline reset and revoke links
stories.story: As a host, I want to close or rotate a compromised link so that I can protect the event.
acceptance: Date and closing window cannot move after first contribution or gift attempt.
Revocation can close earlier and invalidates the old slug.
Lock the event row for date edits and first accepted submission/created gift intent; set window_locked_at atomically and test concurrent attempts to reset deadlines.

epics.title: Manual notes, cards and photos
epics.outcome: Guests can create personal content without AI or a cash gift

stories.title: Write and submit a note
stories.story: As a guest, I want to write my own message so that I can contribute without AI.
acceptance: Text remains editable until submission.
Server validates length, consent and active contribution window.
Persist final text in cards.submissions using same-event guest references and idempotent submission; explicit consent and outbox delivery commit with accepted content.

stories.title: Style a card with templates
stories.story: As a guest, I want to choose a layout, palette and motif so that my card feels personal.
acceptance: A static template is immediately available.
Final text is rendered separately from background art for readability.
Use the same cards.submissions record for note/card kinds; retain template key/version and bounded style JSON instead of duplicating card text or adding an October template catalog.
Review original vector card art, premium typography, full readable long notes and an optional searchable local GIF collection; no generated-image dependency in the core card collection.

stories.title: Submit card without gift
stories.story: As a guest, I want to submit a card without money so that participation is never tied to payment.
acceptance: Card creation does not require a gift ID.
Gift failure cannot remove a submitted card.

stories.title: Attach an optional photo
stories.story: As a guest, I want to attach a photo so that the host can remember the occasion.
acceptance: Enforce type, size and dimension limits and scan uploads.
Private storage and short-lived access URLs are used.
Persist cards.media_assets metadata and private object key; scoped FKs, clean scan state and a partial unique constraint enforce one guest-owned photo per submission.

stories.title: Choose book visibility
stories.story: As a guest, I want to control whether my message appears in the shared book so that my preferences are respected.
acceptance: Consent is explicit and saved with the submission.
Private submissions are excluded from the consented book view.
Persist ordered cards.consent_events with explicit choice and wording version; missing/withdrawn consent denies book inclusion even when the projection is stale.
Increment the submission public source revision and publish a minimal outbox event for later consent changes so stale book projections cannot authorize an export.

stories.title: Hide and remove inappropriate content
stories.story: As a host, I want to moderate guest content so that the book is safe to share.
acceptance: Host can hide or remove an entry with an audit record.
Removal is reflected in later exports.
Append cards.moderation_actions, update content state and publish removal atomically; invalidate existing export artifacts and prevent replay from resurrecting erased data.

epics.title: AI note and artwork assistance
epics.outcome: AI offers bounded editable choices while manual creation always remains available

stories.title: Generate three guided note choices
stories.story: As a guest, I want to select relationship, tone and length so that AI suggests usable notes.
acceptance: Return three distinct short options.
Guest selects and edits one before submission.

stories.title: Accept optional memory without invention
stories.story: As a guest, I want to add a memory so that suggestions feel personal.
acceptance: Treat guest detail as data, not instructions.
With no detail, produce general wording without fabricated memories.

stories.title: Moderate and cap note requests
stories.story: As an operator, I want AI requests bounded so that abuse and cost stay manageable.
acceptance: Validate sessions and event window before provider calls.
Apply input caps, quotas, output validation and refusal fallback.
Persist minimal ai.requests and atomically reserve ai.usage_buckets for guest/event/application caps; concurrent requests cannot exceed limits and failed reservations recover safely.

stories.title: Keep manual composer on AI failure
stories.story: As a guest, I want to finish my note if AI is unavailable so that I am never blocked.
acceptance: Timeout, refusal or malformed output preserves the manual editor.
An AI error does not create or erase a card.

stories.title: Generate two artwork variations
stories.story: As a guest, I want up to two background options so that I can choose a look.
acceptance: One active art job per session and two variations maximum.
Return approved private previews through short-lived URLs.

stories.title: Render readable card typography
stories.story: As a guest, I want names and message text legible so that artwork does not distort them.
acceptance: Place precise text in an HTML or SVG overlay.
Contrast and export rendering match the preview.

stories.title: Budget AI and preserve fallback
stories.story: As a founder, I want request usage measured so that a free pilot does not create runaway costs.
acceptance: Record token/image usage without private memories in logs.
Budget switch disables AI while templates and manual notes continue.
Keep token/image counts, prompt/model versions and outcomes without durable private prompt/suggestion copies; quota counters are not financial transactions.

epics.title: External cash gifts with guest choice
epics.outcome: Guests choose among host-confirmed services and pay the host outside the app

stories.title: Configure several payment services
stories.story: As a host, I want to enable Cash App, Venmo and Zelle together so that guests can choose the service they use.
acceptance: Allow any nonempty subset with one active destination per service.
Only confirmed enabled routes appear to guests.
Persist gifts.routes with UQ (event_id, service) and a scoped current-version reference; enabled plus current host-confirmed version determines guest availability.

stories.title: Double-enter and confirm each identifier
stories.story: As a host, I want to enter each account twice so that I can catch typing errors.
acceptance: Require exact match, format validation, host ownership acknowledgment and review in that service.
Do not accept arbitrary redirect URLs or account credentials.
Persist immutable encrypted gifts.destination_versions; record host confirmation actor/time/wording version once and never store the repeated identifier entry.

stories.title: Pause only a changed service
stories.story: As a host, I want to edit or disable one destination so that other services remain available.
acceptance: Fresh authentication, audit and alert are required.
Edited route disappears until reconfirmed; other confirmed routes continue.
Route edits and handoffs lock the same route row; create a new unconfirmed current version, audit and queue the alert atomically. Prior versions remain historical only.

stories.title: Let guest choose a service
stories.story: As a guest, I want to select from the host’s enabled services so that I can use an app I have.
acceptance: Show only currently confirmed routes.
Selecting another service updates the full recipient and identifier.

stories.title: Reset review when guest switches
stories.story: As a guest, I want a fresh recipient check after switching services so that I do not approve the wrong destination.
acceptance: Changing service or route version clears acknowledgment.
Handoff stays disabled until the selected route is reviewed again.
Increment gifts.gift_intents.review_revision on service/version switches and clear acknowledgment atomically; a stale revision cannot authorize a later handoff.
Keep a handed-off intent’s selected tuple immutable; a later service choice creates a new intent rather than relabeling a prior gift or receipt.

stories.title: Show exact payee before leaving
stories.story: As a guest, I want to see the host-supplied name and exact identifier so that I can compare the recipient in my payment app.
acceptance: Prominent adjacent copy states who supplied the details and that the app has not independently verified them.
Mismatch tells guest to stop and contact host by a known channel.

stories.title: Validate selected route atomically
stories.story: As an operator, I want stale or cross-event gift intents rejected so that a switched or disabled account is not used.
acceptance: Store selected_service, destination_id and version with the intent.
Server rejects stale, disabled, unconfirmed or wrong-event route at handoff.

Use a short PostgreSQL unit of work through public module repositories to lock event/link/session/route/intent and recheck current deadlines, revocation, switches and exact reviewed tuple before recording handoff_issued.
Composite FKs bind event/guest/service/route/version; repeated requests deduplicate durable effects but recheck current authorization and route validity before returning a handoff.

stories.title: Keep external status honest
stories.story: As a guest, I want the app to state what it knows so that a click is not mistaken for a successful payment.
acceptance: Link opened and guest reported remain unverified.
No external handoff is labeled provider verified.
Persist external activity in gifts.gift_events; handoff_issued/guest_reported stay unconfirmed, with no provider settlement, verified transaction or payout ledger in October.

stories.title: Let host mark a checked receipt
stories.story: As a host, I want to mark a gift received after checking that provider account so that my private list is useful.
acceptance: UI labels it host marked received.
Host review records actor and time without claiming provider confirmation.
Append gifts.gift_events host confirmation with actor/time and reviewed version; permit an audited corrective revocation and keep host confirmation distinct from provider verification.
Show guest known name, optional payment-app alias, intended amount, linked card and opaque matching reference. Treat these as unverified clues; names or references alone never establish receipt.

stories.title: Respect gifting deadlines
stories.story: As a host, I want gift initiation blocked after close so that old links cannot be used indefinitely.
acceptance: Active and wedding gift-only states allow new intents.
Final closure rejects new intents while permitting prior reconciliation.
Check the fresh event clock inside the transaction after locking; final closure blocks new handoffs without deleting prior intents or blocking host reconciliation.

stories.title: Investigate approved external transaction-data matching
stories.story: As a host, I want a permitted way to match an external gift to its sender and card so that duplicate names or aliases do not create false receipt claims.
acceptance: Document provider-by-provider personal/business eligibility, available API or approved import, consent/scopes, permitted transaction identifiers, costs and restrictions. Do not assume personal Cash App, Venmo or Zelle history is accessible.

If an approved integration exists, design server-owned event/card/reference mapping with authenticated provider evidence, idempotency, ambiguous-match handling, correction and audit; a browser callback or guest report is not evidence.
Retain known name, payment-app alias, optional amount/reference and manual host receipt review as the fallback. Do not collect credentials, financial screenshots or infer receipt from names alone.
Get owner/provider approval before expanding from external directions to integrated payment processing; keep verified provider state separate from host-confirmed state.

epics.title: Host dashboard, CardVault and event book
epics.outcome: The host keeps private memories and can export them after guest intake closes

stories.title: Show private host dashboard
stories.story: As a host, I want to view entries and gift intent states so that I can manage my event.
acceptance: Host-only view displays approved cards and unverified/host marked gift states separately.
Guest link never grants dashboard access.
Read customer-owned data through public module queries; CardVault is a view of Cards/Gifts data, not a duplicate content table.

stories.title: Create consented event book view
stories.story: As a host, I want a book of allowed notes and photos so that I can revisit them.
acceptance: Book includes only consented and unhidden entries.
A card with an attached photo counts as one entry.
Use book.entry_projection as rebuildable revisioned metadata; obtain content through Cards public contracts and recheck current consent/moderation before disclosure.
Review editorial and collage spreads, a dedication/cover, photo compositions and a readable text mode; preserve complete long notes and remove hidden/nonconsented cards immediately.

stories.title: Export basic CardVault privately
stories.story: As a host, I want a basic export even if I never buy an upgrade so that my memories remain accessible.
acceptance: Host can request export after closure.
Signed download is short-lived and audited.
Persist book.exports with requester, same-event snapshot, status, private object key, expiry and invalidation; never store signed URLs or serve artifacts after removal/withdrawal.

stories.title: Freeze book after day 90
stories.story: As a host, I want a stable snapshot after new entries close so that book pricing and layout can be final.
acceptance: No late wedding gift adds a new book entry.
Snapshot records included count and timestamp.
Persist book.snapshots and book.snapshot_entries after consuming source changes through cutoff; unique membership/position, atomic included count and correction revisions never admit late gifts.

stories.title: Preview book tiers without guest cap
stories.story: As a host, I want the projected $15/$30/$79 price to follow included entry count so that no guest is blocked.
acceptance: Show 0–99, 100–299 and 300+ tiers.
Quote final tier after day 90; no preselected guest list or contribution cap.

stories.title: Honor later removal requests
stories.story: As a guest, I want an allowed removal request to affect later exports so that my content preferences are respected.
acceptance: Host moderation or deletion updates read model and subsequent export.
Required financial records, if any, follow separate retention policy.

epics.title: Security, privacy and reliability
epics.outcome: Authentication, data boundaries and failure tests protect the pilot

stories.title: Authorize every server operation
stories.story: As a host, I want another event’s users blocked from my data so that private content stays private.
acceptance: Validate actor and event from server session, not browser-supplied role.
Cover read, write, export, media and job status routes.

stories.title: Protect browser requests
stories.story: As an operator, I want common web attacks mitigated so that basic routes are not easy to abuse.
acceptance: Use secure cookies, CSRF or strict Origin checks, output escaping and a restrictive CSP.
Test expired sessions and privilege changes.

stories.title: Protect secrets and destinations
stories.story: As a host, I want account identifiers and API keys handled carefully so that exposure is limited.
acceptance: Keep provider secrets server-side; encrypt sensitive destinations at rest.
No bank credentials, passwords or payment details in analytics/logs.
Application-encrypt gifts.destination_versions identifiers and recoverable share secrets with external versioned keys; separate migration/runtime roles and redact database errors/audit/outbox.

stories.title: Limit abuse and uploads
stories.story: As an operator, I want rate limits and file checks so that malicious traffic does not overwhelm the app.
acceptance: Rate-limit session, AI and upload routes.
Reject unsupported/oversized files and scan approved uploads.

stories.title: Test backup and restore
stories.story: As a host, I want my accepted cards recoverable so that an outage does not erase the event.
acceptance: Run tested database backup and restore.
Private media retention and deletion rules are documented.

Document provider/version/backup method and recovery objectives; restore migrated database, private object references and external encryption-key access, then reapply deletion tombstones before serving data.

Publish retention periods/TTLs and a tested manual deletion runbook for sessions, orphan media, exports, customer/guest/content/gift history and replay evidence; event closure alone does not purge CardVault.

stories.title: Make retried work safe
stories.story: As an operator, I want jobs and callbacks to tolerate retries so that duplicate events do not create inconsistent state.
acceptance: Use idempotency keys or unique event IDs.
Replay tests cover duplicate and out-of-order events.

Scope this Post-MVP story to provider callbacks and expanded asynchronous workflows; October SQL idempotency/outbox/consumer foundations belong to DCB-E18-S03 and feature-specific retries stay with their domain stories.

stories.title: Observe failures and spend
stories.story: As a founder, I want error and usage dashboards so that I can detect problems during the pilot.
acceptance: Log minimal event IDs, action outcome, latency and cost.
Alert on auth failures, AI spend and gift-route mismatches without logging private text.

stories.title: Run mobile and accessibility checks
stories.story: As a guest, I want screens I can use on a phone or keyboard so that I can participate at an event.
acceptance: Test focus order, labels, contrast and responsive layouts.
High priority blockers are fixed before supervised pilot.

UI review includes axe WCAG 2.2 AA checks, keyboard skip and route focus, 320/375/768/1280 px reflow, opt-in/pausable GIF motion and real-device/manual assistive-technology review. Automated checks do not certify ADA compliance.

epics.title: Supervised pilot and learning
epics.outcome: Two supervised events validate completion, correct destinations and real demand

stories.title: Recruit pilot hosts
stories.story: As a founder, I want a small set of suitable hosts so that I can test realistic occasions.
acceptance: Recruit 5–10 interested hosts and select two supervised events.
Explain prototype limitations and support contact.

stories.title: Check every published payee
stories.story: As a founder, I want to compare host-entered routes to their payment apps so that wrong destinations are caught before guests use them.
acceptance: Host confirms each enabled account and display name.
Record mismatch and resolution without collecting account credentials.

stories.title: Run scripted money-state tests
stories.story: As a founder, I want wrong-account and closure scenarios tested so that we do not falsely claim gifts were paid.
acceptance: Test switches, stale versions, disabled routes, event boundary and host-marked status.
No unresolved wrong-destination defect at release gate.

stories.title: Measure guest completion
stories.story: As a founder, I want separate conversion for notes, cards and gift handoffs so that I know where users struggle.
acceptance: Record privacy-safe funnel events and mobile failures.
Separate link opens from host-confirmed external receipt.

stories.title: Triage and decide next phase
stories.story: As a founder, I want a release decision based on pilot evidence so that later costs are justified.
acceptance: Review support complaints, usage and premium interest.
Record go/no-go and priority fixes before integrated payments or licensed music.

epics.title: Optional premium cards and books
epics.outcome: Sell optional design upgrades and polished books without charging for basic participation

stories.title: Offer premium card design
stories.story: As a guest, I want to see a $4.99 premium card option so that I can choose a richer design.
acceptance: Free manual path remains.
Premium status and price are clear before checkout.

stories.title: Quote book price from included entries
stories.story: As a host, I want a final server quote so that I pay for the correct $15/$30/$79 tier.
acceptance: Tier uses 0–99, 100–299 or 300+ consented entries after day 90.
Price cannot be altered by the browser.
Quote from a frozen book.snapshots revision and included membership; billing.order_items preserve count/tier/price/currency without another book_orders table.

stories.title: Use hosted product checkout
stories.story: As a buyer, I want to pay for a card or book through a hosted payment page so that the app does not collect my card details.
acceptance: Create server-side order and provider session.
Do not store PAN/CVV or treat return URL as payment proof.
Persist billing.orders/order_items/payment_attempts; customer or same-event guest buyer, unique provider/request references and server prices remain separate from gift funds.

stories.title: Grant paid entitlement on signed event
stories.story: As a buyer, I want access to the upgrade after payment so that I receive what I bought.
acceptance: Verified provider event is replay-safe.
Entitlement applies once to the correct card or event.
Durably deduplicate verified billing.provider_events by provider/event ID and grant billing.entitlements once per paid target; no browser-controlled paid state.

stories.title: Handle failed checkout and refund
stories.story: As a buyer, I want an honest order status so that I know whether I was charged.
acceptance: Pending and failed payments do not unlock.
Refund updates entitlement and purchase history.
Persist billing.refunds against the payment attempt with unique provider refund ID; partial/full refunds preserve purchase history and apply the approved entitlement policy.

stories.title: Track product margins
stories.story: As a founder, I want to compare revenue with processing, AI and media costs so that prices can be adjusted.
acceptance: Report paid conversion by tier and product contribution.
Gift principal is never counted as platform revenue.

epics.title: Approved integrated gift payments
epics.outcome: A provider-approved future route can process gift checkout with a reconciled ledger

stories.title: Secure written provider approval
stories.story: As a founder, I want provider approval for the exact gifting flow so that checkout fits underwriting and legal roles.
acceptance: Document merchant of record, custody, fees, payout timing, disputes and refunds.
Do not enable live integrated gifts before written acceptance.

stories.title: Onboard recipient through provider
stories.story: As a host, I want hosted identity and payout onboarding so that bank details never enter this app.
acceptance: Provider collects documents and bank numbers.
App stores provider account ID and readiness state only.
Persist gifts.recipient_accounts with provider account ID/readiness only, scoped to the customer; no identity documents or bank numbers.

stories.title: Show full fee and create checkout
stories.story: As a guest, I want to see gift, service fee and total before paying so that the charge is clear.
acceptance: Server calculates approved fee and creates idempotent checkout.
Hosted page collects funding credentials.

stories.title: Verify signed payment callbacks
stories.story: As an operator, I want signed webhooks to update payment state so that browser redirects cannot claim a gift was paid.
acceptance: Verify raw payload signature and unique provider event ID.
Duplicate and out-of-order delivery tests pass.
Persist separate gifts.integrated_payments/payment_attempts/provider_events; verified provider-event uniqueness and allowed transitions never promote an external intent to verified payment.

stories.title: Keep gift ledger and payout state
stories.story: As a host, I want available and paid-out totals separated so that I understand where money stands.
acceptance: Settled, payout pending and paid out have distinct states.
Unsettled funds are never shown as available.

Finalize provider-approved gifts.ledger_accounts/ledger_journals/ledger_entries and payouts/payout_allocations design under a new ADR; balanced atomic journals, currency segregation and no mutable host balance.

stories.title: Handle refunds and disputes
stories.story: As an operator, I want reversals recorded so that reported balances remain accurate.
acceptance: Refunds and disputes create compensating entries.
Guest and host views use provider-backed status.
Persist gifts.refunds/disputes with provider references and compensating journals; history is append-only and partial refunds never overwrite settled principal.

stories.title: Reconcile provider and app daily
stories.story: As a founder, I want daily exception reporting so that money mismatches are caught promptly.
acceptance: Compare signed provider events and ledger totals.
Investigate any unmatched charge or payout before expansion.
Persist gifts.reconciliation_runs/items linking provider totals and unmatched payment/payout/journal records with resolution evidence.

stories.title: Retain external route as independent choice
stories.story: As a host, I want approved integrated checkout to coexist safely with external services if supported so that migration is gradual.
acceptance: Clearly distinguish external unverified and integrated provider-verified gifts.
Never merge their statuses or fee models.

epics.title: Conditional music, GIFs and licensed artwork
epics.outcome: Media enriches cards only when the specific distribution rights and cost are approved

stories.title: Obtain music use rights
stories.story: As a founder, I want a contract for short clips so that card and note playback is permitted.
acceptance: Contract covers composition and recording, sharing, territory, term and in-app playback.
Do not assume a 15-second clip is exempt.

stories.title: Offer licensed clip picker
stories.story: As a guest, I want an optional song snippet so that my card evokes a memory.
acceptance: No song is the default; previews play only after a tap.
Store catalog ID and rights version, not a copied recording.

stories.title: Recheck rights at playback
stories.story: As a recipient, I want a card to remain viewable if a song expires so that memories are not lost.
acceptance: Authorize each stream by rights, region and expiry.
Unavailable clip becomes a silent card with allowed attribution.

stories.title: Control audio in exports
stories.story: As a host, I want book exports to honor music rights so that I can share them safely.
acceptance: Default export contains no recorded audio.
Include playback or audio only if export rights are explicitly granted.

stories.title: License art templates and GIFs

epics.title: Database foundations and migrations
epics.outcome: A managed PostgreSQL foundation stores customers, event-scoped guests and honest external gift history with constrained module tables and reliable transactional delivery

stories.title: Validate PostgreSQL deployment and migration workflow
stories.story: As a developer, I want a tested managed PostgreSQL connection and versioned migration workflow so that production persistence can be deployed and recovered safely.
acceptance: Read ADR 0001 and ADR 0005; evaluate Supabase first and record selected provider, supported PostgreSQL version, auth integration, connection adapter, pooling/caching and backup capability after the deployed stack spike passes.

Verify a server-only connection and short multi-statement transaction in the chosen runtime; separate environments and migration/runtime credentials without browser secrets or cached authorization reads.
Establish one ordered module-owned migration history and synthetic-only seed workflow; empty apply, repeat apply and failed-migration recovery pass in an isolated environment.
Do not implement sign-in, event behavior, destination encryption or backup drills here; existing domain/security stories retain those responsibilities.

stories.title: Install module tables and scoped relational constraints
stories.story: As a developer, I want the canonical module tables and constraints so that customer, guest and gift data have one consistent storage contract.
acceptance: Install the 23 October tables in docs/specs/DATA_MODEL.md with module ownership, opaque IDs, typed timestamps/money, same-event FKs, immutable history controls and reviewed indexes.

Enforce unique provider identity, active share link, one photo per submission, one route per event/service and route/current-version references; reject orphan and cross-event guest/media/route/snapshot references with synthetic data.
Persist event-scoped guests separately from sessions; no duplicate hosts/users/customers, notes/cards/CardVault content, generic transaction ledger or future Billing/integrated-payment migrations.
Provide narrow database permissions/policies tested with actual runtime credentials; domain adapters and business behavior remain in DCB-E02 through DCB-E07.

stories.title: Provide atomic units of work and durable delivery
stories.story: As a developer, I want reusable transaction, request deduplication and outbox primitives so that concurrent or retried work cannot lose or duplicate accepted domain changes.
acceptance: Public module repository adapters share a composition-layer PostgreSQL unit of work with documented lock ordering and bounded deadlock/serialization retries; no private-table imports across modules.

Implement platform.idempotency_keys, outbox_messages and consumer_receipts with scoped request digest/resource references, atomic mutation/event commits, leases, bounded retries and source-revision checks.

Demonstrate concurrent same-key submission returns one resource, changed-body key reuse conflicts, rollback leaves no orphan outbox work, and crash/duplicate/out-of-order delivery cannot duplicate or regress a projection.
Domain stories own route/window/quota/consent/receipt checks using these primitives; backup stays DCB-E08-S05 and later provider-specific retry work stays DCB-E08-S06.

Validate CSRF/origin, revisions, bounded input, retry keys, event windows, link rotation, moderation and feature flags on the server; payment execution remains disabled.
Version and test the isolated local SQLite adapter without replacing the managed PostgreSQL/identity production gates; leave private photo uploads visibly unavailable.
Record API/browser verification and local test access; leave GitHub story #90 open and In Progress for owner closure.
